en: The Scripture on the Ritual Manual of the Great Illumination Maṇḍala of the Treasure God, Spoken by the Buddha.
Volume One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao San Da Fu, Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial.
Translated by the Imperial Subject Hōten, the Great Master Dengyō, by imperial decree. Thus have I heard: At one time the Buddha was in the land of Laṅkā.
In that land there were the rākṣasa king Piṅgala and the rākṣasa king Candrasena, and others.
Within the Buddha-dharma, they all attained non-retrogression.
Furthermore, they were respectfully surrounded by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who dwelt in great merit.
At that time, the World-Honored One exercised his supernormal powers.
He ascended into the void and reached the realm of Vaḷabhī;
descending from the sky,
he sat down with composed dignity beneath a *naṅgulu-bījā-maṇi* tree.
At that time, there were the treasure-guarding deity, the yakṣa king, the asura king,
and the mother-cirliṇā nāga king.
The five-crested Gandharva prince Pañcika;
the Rākṣasa king Kumbhīra; the Kinnara king Agniśikha; and the Kinnara king Pañcaśikha.
The yakṣa king Dhanada, the great tree-king kiṃnara,
and furthermore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwelling on the stage of non-retrogression,
with hearts full of great joy, spoke with one voice in unison:
And he said to the Buddha:
"It is rare, World-Honored One! It is rare, Sugata!
That we have now heard for the first time the true Dharma of the great merits of all the Tathāgatas of the past."
Yet all sentient beings suffer immeasurable affliction;
they have no master, no ruler, no savior, and no refuge.
Now this True Dharma can act as their master and ruler, and is able to deliver them.
I only pray that the World-Honored One, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of all sentient beings in the heavens and among humans,
will proclaim this secret maṇḍala ritual manual and heart-mantra.
If sentient beings hear that by practicing the perfection of giving they will attain the complete peace and bliss of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi,
at that time there will further be yakṣas and others.
Rising from his seat, he bared his right shoulder,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms in reverence,
and addressed the World-Honored One, saying: "The Ritual Manual of the Maṇḍala."
"I shall proclaim it for you; listen with a willing heart.
Then the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly, including the yakṣa kings and others: "Listen attentively now, sons of good family, to this True Dharma."
This is the heart-mantra of the ritual manual for the maṇḍala of the Great Yakṣa King;
it is a truly secret teaching, unprecedented and proclaimed by all Tathāgatas in concert.
Furthermore, there were the devaputra Bhaṇi,
the devaputra Mālaha, the devaputra Suma,
the devaputra Viśvasuma, the devaputra Jaya, and others.
At dawn, they all came to where the Buddha was, prostrated with their heads at his feet,
circumambulated him three times, and stood to one side. At that time,
those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, by means of their supernatural powers...
He caused the Nalinī-vijṛmbhita-mālinī tree to emit a great radiance that universally illuminated everything.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed those Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, saying:
"I now wish to proclaim the great ocean of the Dharma, which is magnificent, unprecedented, and perfectly complete.
You all should receive, uphold, believe, follow, and practice it.
At that time, the Yakṣa King Ratnagarbha—
Rising from his seat, he bared his right shoulder,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms in reverence,
and addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One."
"We only pray that, out of compassion, you will explain this true, great ocean of the Dharma— the eightfold unprecedented and perfect dharmas of wealth and prosperity—
which we shall receive, uphold, and practice.
The World-Honored One replied, "So be it."
Regarding the secret dharma of the Great Yakṣa King Mahodara-Padmaprabha-Sarvālaṃkāra:
on both sides of the Great Yakṣa King Ratnagarbha, there are yakṣas.
The first is named Kili, the second is named Mali;
they constantly pour forth from their treasuries of jewels.
In the north are the yakṣa Śyāma, the yakṣa Supūrṇa, and the yakṣa Pūrṇabhadra.
In the east, the yakṣa Labdhārtha and the yakṣa Mahādhana,
as well as the great yakṣa kings Ratnagarbha, Mahodara, and Sarvālaṃkāra,
stood guard at the gate of the Hall of the Sages like youths.
The reciter should visualize these eight great yakṣa kings and then recite the mantras of the retinues of the eight yakṣas: Oṃ dhānana svāhā | Mahādhānana...
Oṃ ākarṣaṇamaṇipataye svāhā | Oṃ pūrṇapratyayapataye svāhā | Oṃ jaganmātṛkṣetrapataye svāhā ||
Vajra-garbha-raśmi-nirhāraya svāhā | Oṃ jvī guṇale nī svāhā | Oṃ kṛle male nī svāhā | These are the eight attendant goddesses.
The King of Vajra-mantras in the east is Pūrṇabhadra; in the south, Vaiśravaṇa;
in the west, Dhana-pati; and in the north, Ratnacūḍa.
These mantra-kings [rule] over all devas, humans, and asuras.
All gave rise to reverence, accepted it with faith, and practiced accordingly.
These eight great yakṣa kings dwell in the rank of Great Bodhisattvas of Sovereignty on the Eighth Ground.
He is well-able to adopt and reject for the sake of benefiting sentient beings;
he dwells securely amidst all the treasures of the triple world,
at the right side of the deity Ratnapāla.
Place a pure precious vase,
as well as Kili Yakṣa and Mali Yakṣa;
these two are the brothers of the deity Vaiśravaṇa, the Lord of Treasures.
He also dwells in the supreme stage of a bodhisattva;
stationed in the southwest corner,
he has vowed to deliver all sentient beings.
First, dwelling in the northeast,
possessing great diligence, perceiving reality, and having made joyful vows of aspiration:
those who recite his name shall obtain whatever they seek.
The Buddha said, "In the past, more than kalpas as numerous as dust motes and ink marks ago, I had deep faith in the Buddha-dharma.
There was a great yakṣa king who invited me in the kingdom of Kāśī to accept the position of consecrated king."
At that time, I entered the maṇḍala and practiced the secret conduct.
For the sake of all sentient beings, I taught the ten wholesome dharmas,
causing those beings to practice the ten wholesome paths together.
Each was able to relinquish all their wealth and possessions.
Thus, I practiced the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā) to its pure fulfillment,
entered the Stage of Joy (pramuditā-bhūmi), and attained the rank of a bodhisattva.
Thereafter, they shall eliminate all the sufferings of poverty and illness for all sentient beings;
they shall seek omniscience and vow to enter the state of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha to attain the wisdom of a Buddha.
The Buddhas of the past were likewise thus.
Having relied upon the teachings of mantra to seek the methods for accomplishment,
they subsequently attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Therefore, Ratnagarbha, Great Yakṣa King, according to the Dharma,
you are the father and mother of all Tathāgatas and the mark of the parinirvāṇa of all Tathāgatas;
you are indeed the Tathāgata who can manifest in the form of a yakṣa.
For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings,
I shall now explain the meaning of the mantra, the maṇḍala ritual, and the procedures for that Great Yakṣa King;
by means of this, if there are practitioners who lack wealth, they shall obtain wealth.
It brings auspiciousness to those who lack it and causes all desired aims to be accomplished.
If one sees or hears this maṇḍala rite of mine, [the same shall occur].
All heavy transgressions committed through ignorance over many kalpas and many lifetimes in the past shall be entirely eliminated.
Furthermore, one will be able to dwell together with and draw near to the Bodhisattva Mahāvidyārāja Ratnapāla.
Before long, they will swiftly attain the stage of non-retrogression,
remaining far removed from all sufferings and afflictions of poverty and low status,
with their bodies and minds in a state of sublime joy.
All those who dwell in the sky— the planets and lunar mansions,
as well as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.
All those with evil minds shall be unable to cause harm, and [this rite] shall provide protection.
These eight great yakṣa kings of immense wealth constitute this vast and perfectly complete Great Dharma Ocean.
If sons of good family and others develop deep faith and,
upholding this unprecedented Dharma, practice the holy life,
the merit they obtain will be no different from that previously described.
At that time, the Great Yakṣa King Ratnagarbha addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One,
these eight kinds of noble and wealthy dharmas are unprecedented."
I now receive and uphold this vow to provide protection, pacify calamities, and bring auspiciousness.
I possess a heart-mantra that is capable of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings.
Out of compassion for this world and for its benefit,
may the Buddha graciously accept [this].
World-Honored One, I now understand this True Dharma.
In past ages, it was mutually transmitted by the Tathāgata Krakucchanda, the Tathāgata Kanakamuni, and the Buddha Kāśyapa.
"I shall now proclaim this heart-mantra.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Great Yakṣa King Ratnagarbha:
"You should speak it quickly; now is the right time."
Having heard the Buddha’s words, the Great Yakṣa King Ratnapāla immediately explained the causes and conditions,
manifesting various transformations as this great yakṣa king.
For example, it is like a great fire that can burn all the fuel of afflictions;
it is like the king among men who is foremost;
and it is like the ocean, which is foremost among all flowing waters.
Among the constellations, the moon is foremost;
this heart-mantra is likewise so.
Within all the four intermediate directions, above, and below—among both the mundane and the supramundane—it is preeminent.
Among those who practice to seek merit, the wealth of virtue and nobility is foremost;
and among the perfectly awakened ones, the World-Honored Ones who are bipeds supreme, both in the heavens and among humans, he is likewise foremost.
At that time, the Great Yakṣa King Ratnagarbha spoke this mantra:
*Namo ratnatrayāya, namo māṇibhadrāya mahāyakṣasenāpataye, oṃ jagatpārajālin-dharāya svāhā.* At that time, the Great Yakṣa King Ratnagarbha...
Having spoken this mantra,
the entire trichiliocosm shook in six ways;
all the yakṣa generals formed mudrās with both hands.
For this mudrā, join the index finger and the thumb together like a chain,
while extending the remaining fingers.
This is called the Garment Seal (*vastramudrā*);
use this mantra: Oṃ dharidhari mahāsammudraṇa-mārādharakāya svāhā. Next, form the Ornamentation Seal (*alaṃkāramudrā*).
With the thumbs of both hands, press against the nails of the remaining three fingers so that each end forms a ring;
then rotate them toward one another.
Next, they are again interlaced;
this is the Seal of Adornment (*alaṃkāra-mudrā*), for which one uses this mantra:
Oṃ miga-varaṇa-jara-jalambu-gana svāhā. Next is the *Vikṣepa* (Waving) Seal.
Form a fist with the right hand and place the left hand on the hip.
This is the *vījana-mudrā* (fanning mudrā); employ this mantra: Oṃ hara hara rājāgra-hara raṇaya svāhā. Next, form the maṇḍala-mudrā.
Join the two hands in *añjali*,
keeping the fingertips open so they do not touch one another,
and let the fingers hang downward.
This is the maṇḍala mudrā.
It is used together with the ritual of anointing the altar. Recite this mantra.
Oṃ kūtāruṇavartita pṛthivī svāhā. Next, form the seal of the five-colored powders.
When spreading the powder maṇḍala,
one should place the five fingers flat and even,
covering them downward upon the ground.
This is the seal for the five-colored powders.
Use this mantra: *Hī hī pīna-male balya-śūbaya svāhā*. Next, form the incense seal.
Form the añjali with both hands;
insert the ring fingers, middle fingers, and index fingers into the palms,
and join the little fingers together like needles.
This is the incense mudrā; use this mantra:
Oṃ rāra kāra sūryaṃ dhanya svāhā. Next, form the flower mudrā.
With the two thumbs held upright and side by side—this mudrā is used for both incense and flowers; the mantra is likewise so.
Now, regarding this ritual procedure:
The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, have also briefly explained this:
if there is anyone who makes offerings to this dhāraṇī,
it is no different from making offerings to all the Buddhas.
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha,
constantly accepts and constantly nurtures those sentient beings who recite this according to the Dharma.
"Swiftly enter the ten stages, cultivate the ten pāramitās, and achieve the ten powers.
At that time, the World-Honored One, while seated upon his throne,
surveyed the great assembly and addressed the Great Yakṣa King Ratnagarbha:
O Treasure God, this maṇḍala ritual manual,
along with its secret mantras and mudrā methods,
has been proclaimed by all the Tathāgatas.
The Tathāgata Vipaśyin, the Tathāgata Śikhin,
the Tathāgata Viśvabhū, the Tathāgata Krakucchanda,
the Tathāgata Kanakamuni, and the Tathāgata Kāśyapa.
Now I, Śākyamuni Tathāgata, shall likewise proclaim it all.
Excellent, Treasure God!
Listen attentively now and reflect upon it well.
For the benefit of all sentient beings in the heavens and among humans, and to increase their roots of virtue,
I shall relate the account of my quest for the Dharma in the past.
Throughout countless eons of the past, I...
He regularly went into the mountains to gather firewood for his livelihood.
One day, while in those mountain wilds, he saw a sick bhikṣu who,
wishing to gather wood, lacked the strength to do so.
Out of a heart of compassion, I gave him firewood,
lit a fire, prepared food, and attended to him;
after one day had passed, that bhikṣu—
His body attained peace and happiness, and his mind was filled with great joy.
He then received from me the three refuges and the five precepts, and was inspired to resolve upon bodhicitta.
Thereafter, I explained to him this maṇḍala ritual for the secret samaya.
At that time, having obtained this King of Mantras,
I contemplated it with single-minded focus and maintained it according to the ritual;
thus, I was able to accomplish all the victorious deeds of the Noble Treasure God.
Perform the homa three times, then perform the water-homa;
thereafter, offer arghya three times a day,
and recite the Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra with single-minded devotion.
Performing the visualization as previously described, seek the Dharma daily;
you will achieve eight kinds of retinues that will constantly protect you.
Furthermore, write down the mantra and wear it around your neck.
One will obtain the protection of the deity Ratnagarbha.
If anyone recites this mantra one hundred thousand times,
or two hundred thousand times, or three hundred thousand times.
Having established banners and streamers before a stūpa containing relics and observed the fast and precepts,
one should perform offerings for three nights for the sake of the yakṣas; thus, one will attain the requested accomplishments,
gaining the supreme supernormal powers and great spiritual might.
Regarding the ritual procedure for water *homa*:
it causes sentient beings to obtain great wealth and treasures.
First, one should observe the fast and precepts at a tranquil location by a river.
Then, enter the water until it reaches the navel;
perform *homa* by offering water with the hands,
and further recite the Ratnabhadra mantra while using scented ointment.
The reciter visualizes:
Ratnabhadra is placed upon the index finger,
and Pūrṇabhadra is placed upon the middle finger.
For the attainment of wealth, place [the mantra] upon the ring finger.
For Vaiśravaṇa, place it in the center of the palm. For *kīrimāṇimantrī mukhena nara śiraśiriṇadara*, place it upon the thumb.
In this way, the noble ones and the holy ones see one another and are able to provide protection.
Thus, the Buddha taught that the ritual manual for the yakṣa maṇḍala possesses such meritorious qualities.
How much more so for the wise person who recites [the sūtras], trusts in the Buddha, reveres the Dharma,
upholds the precepts, is widely learned, and possesses a single-minded purity.
The merit of constructing this supreme maṇḍala is immeasurable.
If one wishes to construct this maṇḍala,
it must be done upon a pure site where there are flowers, fruits, and groves of trees.
Dig the ground to the depth of a knee, with a width of twelve cubits.
Sprinkle it with the five kinds of pure water to consecrate the site.
Then, fill and ram it down until it is as level and smooth as the palm of a hand.
Recite the mantra of the Yakṣa King to perform consecration,
making offerings of various incenses and flowers.
When performing the rite, it must be on an auspicious day during the waxing moon.
The ācārya, with a mind of sincere purity,
performs self-purification by means of the five kinds of pure water.
With single-minded concentration, he recites the King of Mantras to perform protection.
Next, one should establish the boundary for the ten directions, above and below.
Reciting the mantra of the Treasure Store Deity (Ratnagarbha), one consecrates scented water and sprinkles it in sequence to purify the area.
Then, using five-colored threads, one has a young girl weave them together.
Thereafter, having perfumed it with kumuda-fragrant water,
one should use wood from the udumbara tree for stakes and,
using a measuring line, construct the maṇḍala.
First, begin with the eastern direction.
Construct four sides and four corners, opening four gates.
In the center, place the Tathāgata, the King of All-Knowledge, complete with all his marks.
Below, one should install the deity Ratnagarbha,
whose color is like a blue cloud and who is endowed with all the marks,
adorned with various kinds of jewels.
He sat cross-legged upon a lion throne adorned with various jewels,
which emitted such magnificent and great radiance;
his right hand was formed in the mudrā of granting boons.
In his palm is an *āmra* fruit;
in his left hand he holds a precious bag filled with various kinds of jewels.
Furthermore, on both sides of the deity of the treasure-store (Vaiśravaṇa), there are...
One should install two golden yakṣa kings:
the first named Cullanaḍa and the second named Mukhinaḍa;
their physical forms and characteristics are identical.
Below the deity Ratnagarbha,
place the yakṣī Saptamātṛkā and Navamātṛkā;
to the east of the maṇḍala, place the yakṣī Mātṛkā.
In the southeast corner, place Maṇināga;
in the south, place Nāganābha; in the west, place Ambaṣṭha.
In the southwest, one should place Nīlanātha; in the north, Vaiśravaṇa;
and in the northwest, the powerful and wealthy deity Īśāna.
In the northeast is the yakṣa king Vemacitrin, the Great Powerful One; next are the yakṣas Jambhala and Pāñcika.
The yakṣa Susīma, the yakṣa Śvāna, the yakṣa Jambhaka, the yakṣa Mukhara, the yakṣa Raktojjvala, and the yakṣa Mahunara.
On the third tier outside the maṇḍala,
one should next place the yakṣiṇīs;
each must be depicted with a dignified and beautiful appearance.
The yakṣī Vairo, the yakṣī Viśālā, the yakṣī Candraśobhā, the yakṣī Gaurī, the yakṣī Surucirā, and the yakṣī Padmasenā.
The yakṣī Svāpī, the yakṣī Mahāmāyā, the yakṣī Sugrīvī, the yakṣī Dhanañjayā, the yakṣī Puṣkalī, and the yakṣī Naradattā.
He forms the mudrā of bestowing all gifts and making all vows,
as well as Maṇibhadra, Kāmarūpin, Surūpa, Vajrin, Sūnarśani, Mahāgaura, Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, and others.
Either twenty or one hundred [of these] should be placed individually outside the maṇḍala according to their respective directions.
Next, there are the vajra, vajra-sword, vajra-staff, conch, noose, banner, wheel, and trident.
Outside, in the first layer, establish the boundary-net (*sīmā-bandha-jāla*);
in the second layer, again establish vajra-wedges;

and in the third layer, establish blazing vajra-flames, ensuring they encircle [the site] on all sides. Next, I shall briefly explain the ritual procedures for powdering the mandala, summoning the deities, and making offerings.
One must use powders of five colors—blue, yellow, red, white, and black.
First, apply the powder to the ground in the eight directions to form the eight blazing flames and so forth, as previously described.
Next, fashion an *argha* bowl, filling it with scented water and fine flowers.
Recite the heart-mantra of the Yakṣa Ratnagarbha to perform the invocation.
The practitioner must be personally devout and free from doubt regarding yakṣiṇīs and the like.
Each must individually recite their own root mantra to perform the invocation,
thereby summoning the Great Radiant Treasure God (Mahāratnagarbha-deva), the God among Gods, to those who possess virtue and wisdom.
Having thus performed the invocation,
one should [offer] garlands of mālatī flowers, exquisite-colored lotuses,
utpala flowers, and karṇikāra flowers.
Kuraṇṭaka flowers and kiṃśuka flowers,
as well as unguents, incense, lamps, and food offerings—
all necessary items— should be presented in due order.
Next, perform the homa ritual using lac,
frankincense, camphor, and white sandalwood before the presence of Ratnapāṇi.
Perform one thousand *homa* offerings with single-minded devotion.
Place *argha* vases at the four corners of the mandala,
filling them with scented water and adding the five grains and five medicinal herbs.
Furthermore, insert a tree branch into the mouth of the flask and recite this mantra of the deity Ratnagarbha:
*jagatpārañjalin drāya svāhā*. This mantra is capable of accomplishing all tasks.
Furthermore, the Great Yakṣa King Mahāprajñāratnabhadra spoke this Heart Mantra of the Yakṣas:
Oṃ yakṣa svāhā. This mantra is also capable of accomplishing all matters.
The Sūtra on the Ritual Manual of the Maṇḍala of the Great Radiance of the God Ratnagarbha, Spoken by the Buddha, Volume I;
The Sūtra on the Ritual Manual of the Maṇḍala of the Great Radiance of the God Ratnagarbha, Spoken by the Buddha,
Volume II.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmadeva, Imperially Appointed Court Dispersing Grandee and Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, and Great Master of the Transmission of the Teaching, under Imperial Decree; here follow the mantras of the various sections.
The rites for invitation, dismissal, offering, and consecration are all universally applicable. *Ānanda padmāya svāhā*. This is the mantra of the Lotus Treasure.
*Ānanda śaṅkhāya svāhā*. This is the mantra of the Śaṅkha Jewel-treasury.
*Rājñāpāyadharādhipataye svāhā*. This is the mantra of the Yakṣa King Rājñāpāya.
Maṇināpavadanadipate svāhā. This is the mantra of the Yakṣa King Ratnanābha.
*Sunābhaya yakṣādhipataye svāhā*. This is the mantra of Sunābha, the Yakṣa King.
*Ambaṇābhaya-dhanadite svāhā*. This is the mantra of Ambaṇābha Yakṣarāja.
Nirṇayāya dhanadipataye svāhā. This is the mantra of the yakṣa king Nirṇaya.
VAIŚRAMAṆĀYA DHANADĪPATAYE SVĀHĀ. This is the mantra of Vaiśravaṇa, the King of Yakṣas.
MAHĀNĀGAYAKṢARĀJADHIPATYE SVĀHĀ. This is the mantra of Mahānāga Yakṣarāja.
Harañjaka-bhaga hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. This is the mantra of Harañjaka, the yakṣa king.
Jagat-pāka-ya-candra-ya svāhā. This is the mantra of the yakṣa king Jagatpāka.
HŪṂ HŪṂ NĀNASŪKṢETRAJĀYA SVĀHĀ. This is the mantra of the yakṣa king Sūkṣetrāja.
Hara hara caṇḍasiṃhāya svāhā. This is the mantra of Caṇḍasiṃha, the yakṣa king.
*jyavanāya svāhā*. This is the mantra for *homā* (fire sacrifice).
When performing the *homā*, one should use wood from the *apāmārga* plant.
Anoint the tips of these firewood sticks with ghee, curd, and honey;
observe the precepts for one day and night,
and perform eight thousand homa offerings.
One will attain great intelligence;
it enables the reciter to memorize one thousand verses daily and never forget them.
If one fashions an image of the deity Vasupūjya from the root of the arka tree, [the same result is achieved].
It may be six finger-widths in length;
its head is adorned with a celestial crown of various ornaments.
One should make offerings of incense and flowers.
However, using *apāmārga* wood as fuel,
dip it into ghee, curd, and honey,
and perform one hundred thousand (*lakṣa*) *homa* offerings.
Every day one obtains one hundred silver coins.
Furthermore, recite the heart-mantra of the Treasure God (Ratnapāla):
*Namo ratnatrayāya | namo maṇibhadrāya mahāyakṣasenāpataye | svāhā svavikṛṇe mṛtici svāhā.* This is the heart-mantra of the Treasure God.
One will be able to attain the supreme accomplishment.
If one enters water up to the knees and performs a water-homa while reciting this mantra, one can obtain wealth and profit. Furthermore, if one uses nimba wood...
It should be four finger-widths long and made level and straight.
One who maintains the precepts should paint the image of Ratnabhadra, complete with all its ornaments.
Having made offerings of food, drink, and so forth, [one should proceed].
Three times each day, using fire that produces much smoke and little flame,
perform eight thousand *homa* offerings with lacquer resin (*śilājatu*).
It can subdue the great lords of wealth.
Furthermore, it is taught that the heart-mantra (hṛdaya-mantra) of another yakṣa king, with its syllables complete,
can also cause one to attain the most supreme accomplishment.

*Ratna-pratītyasamutpāda-samaya-manusmara-maṇi-pratārāya vāg-vadhu-ajita-sādhu-dhama-dhama-mañjira-mahā-yakṣa-seṇā-pilinda-turu-turu-maṇi-pratāra-turu-turu-maṇi-pratāra-koṭi-koṭi-maṇi-pratāra-toṭi-toṭi-maṇi-pratāra-teṭi-teṭi-maṇi-pratāra svāhā.* Furthermore, there is another ritual for the maṇḍala that does not require selecting auspicious stars or days.
Nor does it require one who maintains the precepts;
one need only use *ariṣṭa* wood, *nimba* wood, or other types of wood to fashion the image of Ratnaketu.
Make offerings with incense and flowers.
At midday, use white mustard seeds and vegetable oil to smear them upon the body of the image of Ratnapāṇi.
Recite the aforementioned mantra one hundred thousand times;
you will obtain eight coins daily,
and once obtained, they must be spent immediately.
"One must not keep even a single coin; one should do this every day.
The Treasure-Guarding Deity further expounded the mantra ritual, instructing that the practitioner first beg for food and observe the fast before reciting the mantra.
Recite the root mantra three hundred thousand times (*tri-lakṣa*).
Thereafter, arrange a great offering before the Tathāgata;
by reciting the mantra eight thousand times, one will obtain abundant wealth.
Next, the water-homa (udakahoma) is explained: every day, one should scoop up water with the hands and pour it back down into the water.
Continue in this manner until one hundred or one thousand scoops have been made.
By making offerings before the noble and holy ones in this manner for six months, one will be able to obtain great wealth.
Next, the mantras for the empowerment of the various families for entering the Great Maṇḍala are taught.
Jra-gaṃ-bha-na-ṭa-mu-ṭa-kā-ya svāhā. This is the mantra of the yakṣiṇī Muṭakā.
Rak-ta-ji-va svāhā. This is the mantra of the yakṣiṇī Rakta-jīvā.
*Mahuranarāya svāhā*. This is the mantra of the yakṣiṇī Mahuranarā.
*Vimara vimara naliśani āhye svāhā*. *Vimara vimara viśrāṇaya nimodāya svāhā*. This is the mantra of the yakṣiṇī Vimaraviśrā.
Candraśumati candrai candra-mate svāhā. This is the mantra of the yakṣī Candraśumati.
*Avahani-sulocanā oṃ jvalana-patnī svāhā | Patnī-sarasvatī-mānuṣī svāhā | Subhū-vāg-bhāratī svāhā | Vāgvāhini-male ghaṭa-kucche svāhā.* These are the mantras of Mahāmāyā, the yakṣī, and the others.
Sukhi śamale kṣapaṇi svāhā. This is the mantra of the yakṣī Sukhīśā.
VAṆMA LE MA LE NI SVĀHĀ. This is the mantra of the yakṣiṇī Manoramā.
ULI ṬI ṢṬHA PUṢKALE SVĀHĀ. This is the mantra of the yakṣiṇī Puṣkalā.

Nṛmamale kagle hṛle nṛme kile kile svāhā | Kāmamale nīlasiddhe svāhā | Kāmamale sarvanirvāsasarvagaramanujavibhāgavate svāhā | Manujavākāmārupe vibhāṇi svāhā | These are the mantras of the yakṣīs, beginning with Kāmārupe.
Srutavajriṇī-khaṅgali-svāhā. This is the mantra of the yakṣiṇī Srutavajriṇī.
SUNARŚANI KĀMINI SVĀHĀ. This is the mantra of the yakṣiṇī Sunarśanā.
*Mahogra-ārya-bhagali-svāhā*. This is the mantra of the yakṣiṇī Mahogra. *Indrāya devādhipataye svāhā*. This is the heart-mantra of Śakra.
Agnaye havyavāhāya svāhā. This is the mantra of the Fire Deity.
Yāmyabṛhatīpataye svāhā. This is the heart-mantra of the Yāma heaven.
Then he recited: *Nairṛtye laukikeśvari svāhā*. This is the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya-mantra*) of Nairṛti.
*Vāruṇāya jvaladibhūtaye svāhā*. This is the heart-mantra of the deity Varuṇa.
*Vāyave 'nadhṛkṣadibhūtaye svāhā*. This is the heart-mantra of the deity Vāyu.
Kuvirāya dhana-pataye svāhā. This is the heart-mantra of Kuvira.
Iśānāya dhanadhipataye svāhā. This is the heart-mantra of Iśāna-deva.
Jālidhamani svāhā. This is the heart-mantra of Mahābrahmā.
*Āmaviṣṇave svāhā*. This is the heart-mantra of Nārāyaṇa. *Anivartitānaya svāhā*. This is the heart-mantra of Vajra.
Haraṭa-sānāya svāhā. This is the heart-mantra of the spear (śakti).
Mahāśyāmāya svāhā. This is the heart-mantra of the staff (daṇḍa).
*Khaṅgavimaladhāriṇi svāhā*. This is the heart-mantra of the sword.
*Varuṇavāmaya svāhā*. This is the heart-mantra of the noose.
*Pra-pu-kañja-nāya svāhā*. This is the heart-mantra of the banner (*dhvaja*).
*Mahā-saumyā-raśma-ye svāhā*. This is the heart-mantra of the wheel (*cakra*).
*Vajra-vajriṇi-āveśa-gre svāhā*. This is the heart-mantra of the trident (*triśūla*), used together with the boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*).
*Saraṇāya svāhā*. This is the mantra of the bow and arrow.
*Oṃ jvalitajvālāvartāya svāhā*. This is the mantra of the vajra-net.
In this manner, each of the respective mantras of the deities is recited to empower the auspicious vase (kalaśa).
Then, for all the disciples who enter the maṇḍala:
Using this auspicious vase, one bestows the empowerment,
causing the recipient to attain wealth, nobility, and good fortune.
If they enter the great maṇḍala...
With a sincere mind, one receives the empowerment according to the Dharma with devotion;
furthermore, one will be able to behold the deity Ratnagarbha and,
through his threefold instructions, master the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā).
Furthermore, perform *homa* and present extensive offerings with twenty kinds of substances.
Recite the root mantras of the Noble Deity and the Great Yakṣa King.
Offer worship according to one's ability three times each day.
Having attained the supreme accomplishment of the samādhi-mantra for one’s own protection, the Buddha said:
"I shall now further explain the methods of the supreme mudrās and the mantra syllables for the perfection of one's practice."
At that time, the great yakṣa kings and others,
their hearts filled with longing and devotion, requested the Buddha to proclaim this teaching.
Then the World-Honored One surveyed the entire great assembly.
He let out a lion’s roar and declared:
"Listen closely, listen closely!
This Dharma of the mantra and mudrā of the deity Ratnagarbha is endowed with great compassion."
He is able to subdue those who are difficult to tame.
He brings about the accomplishment of all beneficial matters for all sentient beings.
The yakṣa kings and others touch their right knees to the ground.
With palms joined toward the Buddha, they listened in silence.
At that time, the World-Honored One,
like a great lion, spoke with sovereign fearlessness regarding mantras and mudrās.
The two palms are placed flat together side by side;
the two middle fingers are interlaced,
and the two ring fingers are like needles.
Bend the third phalanges of both index fingers;
join the two index fingers to the ring fingers,
and let the thumbs rest along the index fingers.
The two little fingers are like needles;
this is the fundamental mudrā of the Treasure Store Deity (Ratnagarbha).
This mudrā is formed by joining the middle [fingers].
The deity Ratnagarbha will manifest before one;
by observing the practitioner who recites this mantra, he will grant the accomplishment of their aspirations. Recite this mantra.
Namo ratnatrayāya | Namo māṇibhadrāya mahāyakṣasenāpataye | Oṃ jvala rañjara lindra svāhā. This is the mantra and its mudrā.
Apply it to five places on one's own body.
When performing this rite, that practitioner becomes like the deity Vaiśravaṇa himself.
Next, perform the mudrā of Vajranara Yakṣarāja:
clench both hands into fists with the little fingers extended like needles,
and recite this mantra.
Oṃ calendrāya svāhā. This mantra-seal can cause the Yakṣa King to provide protection.
Next, form the mudrā of the Yakṣa King Mukhaccheda:
clench the hands into fists with the little fingers tucked into the palms,
and extend the ring fingers like needles while reciting this mantra.
Oṃ mukheṇdra-ya svāhā. This mantra-seal can also provide protection for the reciter.
Next, perform the mudrā of all yakṣiṇīs:
insert the little fingers into the palms and bend the third joints of the ring fingers.
Recite this mantra:
Oṃ ani... This mantra-seal can also provide protection and may be used for invocation.
Next, perform the mudrā of the maṇḍala wall:
clench both hands into fists,
with each index finger extended like a needle.
Recite this mantra:
Oṃ caruṇḍara bandha nigrahe phaṭ. Next, perform the net-seal (jāla-mudrā) on the upper part of the maṇḍala.
Reverse the previous seal so that the two index fingers join together like a needle.
Recite this mantra:
Oṃ mukhacintāmaṇi hūṃ phaṭ. Next, perform the mudrā of the maṇḍala-kīla:
form fists with both hands.
Lowering the hands toward the ground, recite this mantra:
Oṃ hāri. Next is the mudrā for summoning the seven retinues.
As before, bend the thumbs of the root mudrā and recite this mantra:
*Oṃ he he julu julu jvalasāyanapriye svāhā*. Such is the ritual procedure.
This will cause the seven retinues to assemble.
Next, perform the ritual offering of water for the arghya by cupping the hands together.
Place the thumb and index finger against the middle finger and recite this mantra:
Oṃ bhaiṣajyasya nāthāya dhanapriye paśya paśya svāhā. Next, perform the seat-offering mudrā.
Join the palms and raise the hands so that the third joints of the three pairs of fingers are bent;
spread the middle fingers apart, with each thumb separated from the others.
This is the Lion Throne mudrā of the deity Ratnagarbha.
Forming this mudrā in the center,
the Yakṣa King together with his retinue sit upon a lion throne;
for all aspirations, one should recite this mantra.
Oṃ jaganbara-jinendra ina-masana-mṛga svāhā. Next, perform the mudrā for bathing.
To invite the deity Ratnagarbha along with his retinue for a ritual bath:
form the gesture of cupping with both hands,
with the little fingers interlaced.
The two ring fingers are placed within the palms;
the two middle fingers are like needles;
and the two index fingers are attached to the third joints of the middle fingers.
The thumb is also placed against the index finger while reciting this mantra:
Oṃ saṃnābhiriya ghaṭa ghaṭa kuṃbharāja svāhā. Next, perform the mudrā for offering the robe.
Place the two hands side by side as if holding a garment, and recite this mantra:
*Nīlatārākṣasadīptāyai svāhā*. Then, recite the mantras of the various families in succession to dispatch the noble deities.
Vāruṇāya kūbaradipataye svāhā | Vāyave viṃcadrikṣadipataye svāhā | Kuberāya dhanadipataye svāhā ||
Namaḥ īśānāya budhnyāya svāhā | Urdhvāya mārīcāya svāhā | Māveṣaṇavisa svāhā | Āḥ ||
Vamantakāya svāhā | Vajrāṅkuśāya svāhā | Śaktaye svāhā | Māyāya svāhā | Nanda-khaḍga-vimala-cūḍe svāhā.
Nisvāhā varuṇa-tamari-vāhe svāhā | pāśaprabhugraṇāya svāhā | dvaja-mahāsomyāra ||
Sāmaye svāhā | Karmarabhyagale svāhā | Trailokyamabhyagale svāhā | Niṣpannasāraṇa ||
